propositions: Link writes are relation-scoped (keyed on target_id + relation), allowing one pair to hold multiple differently-related deps simultaneously, but removal is pair-scoped and takes no relation argument, causing permanent non-convergence when guard G5 declines a mismatched removal.

The reconciler's inbound link-removal path reaches guard G5 when outbound differs emit no link mutation (inbound-only pass or vendor-type deduping), survives inbound removal suppression, and re-emits+re-declines every pass for double-related pairs.

Making removal symmetric with writes by keying on (target_id, relation) allows the reconciler to converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation instead of declining forever, while preserving the safety invariant that no peer-active link is removed.

The public CLI and library API remain backward-compatible: rebar unlink <id1> <id2> with no relation argument retains existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior, while an optional relation argument enables relation-scoped removal.
